questions.q: Benzene is treated with Na in liquid NH₃ containing ethanol. The product is:
questions.explain: Electron, proton, electron, proton: the two new hydrogens add para to each other, leaving two isolated C=C bonds. The conjugated 1,3-diene is the common trap, and the ring is not reduced further.

questions.q: The Birch reduction of anisole, C₆H₅OCH₃, gives:
questions.explain: Protonation occurs ortho to an electron donor, so OCH₃ stays on a carbon of a remaining double bond. Ethers are not cleaved under Birch conditions.

questions.q: Benzoic acid is reduced with Na/liquid NH₃ and an alcohol. The product is:
questions.explain: An electron-withdrawing group ends up on the sp³ carbon, where it stabilises the neighbouring carbanion, so protonation is para to COOH. The COOH group itself is not reduced.

questions.q: Dec-5-yne is treated with Na in liquid NH₃. The product, and the reagent that would give its geometric isomer, are:
questions.explain: The vinyl radical flips freely, and the vinyl anion forms in the less hindered trans shape, so Na/NH₃ gives the E-alkene. H₂ with Lindlar catalyst gives the cis-alkene.
